chunks: The eminent Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Bukran al-Naqqash narrated to us in Kufa. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us from his father, from Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said:

Surely, the first thing that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created to teach His creation writing was the letters of the alphabet. If a man is struck on his head with a staff and it is claimed that he cannot articulate some words, then the ruling is that the letters of the alphabet be presented to him, and the blood money is paid in proportion to what he cannot articulate of them. And indeed my father narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), regarding the alphabet (Alif Ba Ta Tha). He said:

The Alif stands for the bounties of Allah. The Ba for the delight of Allah. The Ta for the perfection of the Order through the Qa'im of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). The Tha for the reward of the believers for their righteous deeds. The Jim for the beauty and majesty of Allah. The Ha for the forbearance of Allah toward the sinners. The Kha for the obscurity of the people of sin before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The Dal for the religion of Allah. The Dhal for the One of Majesty and Nobility. The Ra for the Kind, the Merciful. The Zay for the earthquakes of the Resurrection. The Sin for the splendor of Allah. The Shin for: Allah willed what He willed and decreed what He decreed, and you do not will except that Allah wills. The Sad for the Truthful in promise in carrying the people over the Path and trapping the transgressors at the lookout. The Dad for: whoever opposes Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad has gone astray. The Ta for Tuba for the believers and a goodly reward. The Dha for the good impression the believers have of Allah and the poor impression the disbelievers have of Him.

The Ayn stands for the Knower. The Ghayn for the Needless. The Fa for a crowd from the crowds of the Fire. The Qaf for: the collection and recitation of the Quran are upon Allah. The Kaf for the Sufficient. The Lam for the slander of the disbelievers in their fabrication of lies against Allah. The Mim for the mastery of Allah on a Day when there is no mastery but His, and Allah says: 'To whom belongs the mastery this Day?' Then the spirits of His prophets, His messengers, and His Proofs will say: 'For Allah, the One, the Triumphant.' Then Allah will say: 'This Day, every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. No injustice today! Surely, Allah is swift in account.' The Nun for what Allah will give the believers and His torment of the disbelievers. The Waw for: woe to whoever disobeys Allah. The Ha for: humiliation before Allah upon whoever disobeys Him. The Lam-Alif for: there is no god but Allah, the word of sincerity - there is no servant who says it sincerely except that Paradise becomes obligatory for him. The Ya for: the hand of Allah is above His creation, distributing sustenance - glory be to Him and exalted be He above what they associate.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: Surely Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed this Quran with these letters that all the Arabs use. Then he said: 'If mankind and the Jinn gathered to produce the like of this Quran, they would not produce its like, even if some of them were helpers to others' [17:88].

key_terms.الدية: Blood money (diyah) - compensation paid for bodily harm in Islamic law
key_terms.الصراط: The Path (Sirat) - the bridge over Hell in Islamic eschatology
key_terms.القائم: The Qa'im - the awaited one who will establish divine order (Imam Mahdi)
key_terms.حروف المعجم: Letters of the alphabet - the foundational elements of Arabic writing
key_terms.كلمة الإخلاص: Word of sincerity - the declaration la ilaha illa Allah (there is no god but Allah)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual meanings of the Arabic alphabet letters according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Rida from Imam Ali (peace be upon them), presents a profound esoteric interpretation of the Arabic alphabet, assigning each letter a divine attribute or theological concept. It opens with a legal ruling about assessing speech impairment using the alphabet, then reveals the spiritual meanings: from Alif (divine bounties) to Ya (divine providence). The teaching includes multiple Quranic quotations and was delivered in the scholarly context of 4th-century Shia learning circles in Qum.
